protocol.description:
The transient output protocol can be used by privileged clients to create independent virtual outputs that will be removed from the compositor when the client destroys the object.
This protocol is intended for use with output capture protocols such as "ext_output_image_capture_source_manager_v1" for remoting use-cases.
The "wl_output" global created by this protocol is not tied to a particular hardware device.

interface.name: ext_transient_output_manager_v1
interface.description: The transient output manager creates short-lived outputs.

request.name: create
request.description: Create a new output that is removed when the client side transient output object is destroyed.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the manager.
All objects created by the manager will remain valid until they are destroyed themselves.

interface.name: ext_transient_output_v1
interface.description:
Initially, the transient output is unconfigured. The client should send an initial commit sequence by sending any number of set_* requests followed by a commit request. If the set_buffer_size request is not sent, the compositor will pick a default size, possibly based on user preference or other compositor policy.
Upon receiving the initial commit, the compositor will either accept or deny the request. If accepted, a created event is sent. Otherwise, a denied event is sent.
Once created, a transient output may be reconfigured by sending a new commit sequence.
When the transient output handle is destroyed, the output itself will also be destroyed. The underlying output may be destroyed before the client destroys the transient output handle, in which case the transient output object becomes inert.

request.name: commit
request.description:
Atomically commit all pending changes.
The first time this request is sent, the compositor will reply with either a created or a denied event. Subsequent commits update the output configuration.

request.name: set_app_id
request.description:
Set an application identifier for the transient output.
The app ID identifies the general class of applications to which the transient output belongs.
This request is double-buffered, see the commit request.

request.name: set_sink_tag
request.description:
Set an opaque tag identifying the transient output's endpoint.
The tag identifies the output sink rather than the output path. That is, the tag identifies the destination of the output contents. In other words, the tag should not change if the same destination is reached via a different path (for instance, when plugging a physical display device via a different connector, or when reaching the same machine via a different IP address).
To the best extent possible, the client should pick a stable and distinct tag. Stable means that the tag should not change between reboots, configuration updates, software upgrades and hardware hotplugs. Distinct means that two separate outputs created by the same application should not share the same tag if possible. In practice, picking strictly unique and stable tags may not be possible (e.g. when derived from an EDID), which is why these requirements are best-effort.
The tag may be used to store on-disk preferences for the output.
This request is double-buffered, see the commit request.

request.name: set_description
request.description:
Set a human-readable description identifying the transient output.
The description is a UTF-8 string with no convention defined for its contents. The description needs not be unique. Examples might include 'Foocorp 11" Display' or 'Remote example.org desktop via VNC'.
This request is double-buffered, see the commit request.

request.name: set_buffer_size

description.summary: set the size of the output buffer

request.description:
Set the size of the output buffer in pixels.
This request is double-buffered, see the commit request.

event.name: created
event.description:
This event advertises the global name for the wl_output to be used with wl_registry.bind.
It is sent exactly once, immediately after the transient output is initially configured and the new "wl_output" global is advertised, if and only if the creation of the transient output was allowed.
The compositor may destroy the underlying output at any point. In this case, this object becomes inert and a wl_registry.global_remove event is sent with the "wl_output" global's name.

event.name: denied
event.description:
The event informs the client that the compositor denied its request to create a transient output.
It is sent exactly once, immediately after the transient output is initially configured, if and only if the creation of the transient output was denied.
After receiving this event, the client should destroy the object.

request.name: destroy
request.description: When the transient output object is destroyed by the client, the associated output created by the compositor is also destroyed.
